newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stop EMU delay talk - Germany's Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Stop EMU delay talk - Germany's Kinkel.

text.p: Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Sunday rounded on German eurosceptics calling for the European Union's planned single currency to be postponed.
Kinkel said in a statement that European economic and monetary union (EMU) would start on time in 1999, and any talk of a delay would harm the German economy.
"No one should be in any doubt: The euro must and will come on time on January 1, 1999, and the agreed stability criteria will be strictly observed," Kinkel said.

HE attacked a call by Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber to delay EMU by two years if countries failed to meet the entry targets set out in the Maastricht treaty. Stoiber says that would still leave time to issue euro as cash as planned in 2002.
Kinkel said: "Talking all the time about a delay to the euro...creates uncertainty and turbulence. We can't afford either."
"The signals coming from Germany must be clear to our European partners," Kinkel said. "We Germans cannot come under the suspicion that we want to bale out."
